name: WAINER APTER, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the 1997 amendment did not violate ex post facto protections because the 1948 Act, in effect when Krug committed his crime, also allowed consideration of all relevant information, thus not increasing his punishment.

name: JUSTICE NORIEGA
description: Dissented, argued that the 1979 Parole Act established a social compact for parole conditions, and the retroactive application of the more restrictive 1997 amendment violated ex post facto principles by increasing the risk of prolonged incarceration.

name: PATTERSON, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Daniel's Law is narrowly tailored to protect public officials from harm and reprisal, upholding the law against a journalist's free speech challenge.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: JUSTICES FASCIALE
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: HOFFMAN
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: RABNER, CHIEF JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court's decision to decline empaneling a special grand jury and suppressing a potential presentment was premature, as no actual presentment existed, and the State has the right to proceed with its investigation.

name: GILSON, P.J.A.D.
description: Concurred, argued that N.J.S.A. 19:13-8 is constitutional under the Anderson-Burdick interest-balancing test, as it imposes only a minimal burden on rights and serves the state's compelling regulatory interests in election integrity and political stability.

name: JUSTICE FASCIALE
description: Concurred, argued that the charity care program is not an unconstitutional taking because it does not physically appropriate property, nor is it a regulatory taking given the highly regulated nature of the hospital industry and the paramount public interest it serves.

name: RABNER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the regulation is unconstitutionally overbroad because its broad sweep chills constitutionally protected speech, extending indefinitely and lacking clear guidance or assurances against repercussions.

name: WAINER APTER
description: Concurred, argued that the witness tampering statute is not facially overbroad but may have been unconstitutionally applied to the defendant, requiring vacation of the conviction and a new trial.

name: WAINER APTER
description: Concurred, argued that a mens rea of recklessness (defined as morally culpable conduct involving a deliberate decision to endanger another) is constitutionally sufficient for true threats, and an objective standard (reasonable person similarly situated to the victim) is also required, along with unanimous jury agreement on the specific statutory violation.

name: JUSTICE PIERRE-LOUIS
description: Concurred, arguing that a generalized smell of raw marijuana does not justify a search of every compartment of an automobile, and the search of the engine compartment and trunk exceeded the scope of the automobile exception.

name: RABNER, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that first-time in-court identifications are inherently suggestive and risk depriving defendants of due process rights, and that continuous narration of video evidence by an investigator who did not witness the event is improper.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Concurred, arguing that law enforcement must adhere to the heightened protections of the wiretap acts for prospective electronic communications, not just probable cause, to safeguard individual privacy rights.

name: JUSTICE FASCIALE
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: JUDGE SABATINO
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: JUSTICE FASCIALE
description: Concurred, argued that the circumstances leading to probable cause for the warrantless search were not "unforeseeable and spontaneous" as required by State v. Witt, thus a warrant was necessary.

name: JUSTICE SOLOMON
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: JUDGE SABATINO
description: Did not participate in the decision.

name: FASCIALE, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Court must establish a new procedural and analytical framework to balance a sexual assault victim's confidential communications with a defendant's right to a meaningful defense, setting a heightened discovery standard for pre-incident mental health records.

name: JUSTICE ALBIN
description: Concurred, argued that the attorney-review requirement of N.J.S.A. 25:1-5(h) for palimony agreements violates the substantive due process guarantee of the New Jersey Constitution by interfering with individual autonomy and the right to contract without compelled legal counsel.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Concurred, arguing that the statutory framework for sentencing juveniles, without a review mechanism, contravenes the State Constitution, and a 20-year look-back period is necessary to save the statute from constitutional infirmity.

name: JUSTICE SOLOMON
description: Dissented, arguing that the majority's imposition of a 20-year lookback period for juvenile offenders was a subjective policy decision that overstepped the judiciary's role and should be left to the Legislature.

name: JUSTICE PIERRE-LOUIS
description: Concurred, arguing that fundamental fairness under the New Jersey Constitution prohibits judges from enhancing sentences based on conduct for which a jury acquitted a defendant, as it nullifies the jury's verdict and undermines due process.

name: JUSTICE ALBIN
description: Concurred, arguing that under the New Jersey Constitution, an arrestee has a reasonable expectation of privacy in a police station call without notice of recording, and such recordings require a warrant or consent.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Concurred, argued that the statute should be interpreted narrowly to require legibility and identifiability of license plate markings, and that the 'reasonable mistake of law' doctrine should not be adopted under the New Jersey Constitution to protect individual rights against unreasonable searches and seizures.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Concurred, argued that the defendant's constitutional right to a fair trial was violated by implicit or unconscious racial bias in the jury selection process, particularly through the State's selective criminal history check on a prospective juror.

name: JUSTICE ALBIN
description: Concurred, argued that the virtual grand jury format, as a temporary measure during a public health crisis, preserves the constitutional right to a grand jury presentation without sacrificing core principles, and the Court has the authority to implement such procedures.

name: CHIEF JUSTICE RABNER
description: Concurred, argued that the CJRA focuses on a defendant's voluntary actions and does not authorize detention based on the risk of removal by immigration authorities.

name: JUSTICE ALBIN
description: Dissented in Lopez-Carrera, arguing that the majority's decision infringes on the State's sovereign power to prosecute and victims' rights by preventing detention of non-citizens facing certain and imminent removal by ICE; concurred in Molchor and Rios as their removals were not certain and imminent.

name: JUSTICE PIERRE-LOUIS
description: Dissented in Lopez-Carrera, arguing that the majority's decision infringes on the State's sovereign power to prosecute and victims' rights by preventing detention of non-citizens facing certain and imminent removal by ICE; concurred in Molchor and Rios as their removals were not certain and imminent.

name: JUSTICE PATTERSON
description: Concurred, argued that the release time provisions in the collective negotiations agreement are authorized by statute and do not violate the Gift Clause of the New Jersey Constitution, serving a public purpose.
